Damage Mechanisms in Saudi Service — Sulfidation, HTHA, CUI, Sour, Chloride

Saudi service drives a specific damage-mechanism stack per API RP 571: sulfidation §4.4.2 (Aramco refining trains, parabolic rate curves on carbon steel above 230°C); naphthenic-acid corrosion §4.4.7 (heavy-crude trains at Ras Tanura, Yanbu); HTHA §5.1.3.1 (every hydrocracker, Nelson curves per API RP 941); amine cracking §5.1.2.3 (acid-gas removal across Hawiyah, Berri, Khurais gas plants, NACE SP0472 PWHT triggers); sour-water cracking §5.1.2.4 + NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 hardness limits on sour-service piping; CUI §4.3.5 (Yanbu + Ras Tanura coastal salt-laden air); chloride SCC §4.5.1 (austenitic stainless brine + cooling-water service); MIC §5.1.1.6 (stagnant sea-water cooling Red Sea + Arabian Gulf); HIC/SOHIC §5.1.2.4 on sour-service vessels. Atlantis cohorts drill closed-book damage-mechanism recognition against live macrographs from Aramco / SABIC turnarounds.
